# Zotero JS Bridge

> A Zotero plugin that exposes eight local HTTP endpoints on Zotero's own `127.0.0.1:23119` server, letting a script run JavaScript inside a live Zotero process — merge duplicate items, query the library, bulk-edit metadata, read logs, and take backups.

This file is a hand-written index for language models, following the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) convention. The full text of every document listed here is also concatenated into [`llms-full.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/llms-full.txt), which is generated by `build_llms.py` and must not be edited by hand.

Key facts:

- **Eight endpoints**, all on Zotero's existing server. Nothing new is bound and no socket is held, so Zotero still exits cleanly.
- **Four write**: `/zoterojs/exec`, `/zoterojs/merge`, `/zoterojs/apply`, `/zoterojs/enrich`. **Four are read-only**: `/zoterojs/ping`, `/zoterojs/logs`, `/zoterojs/query`, `/zoterojs/doctor`.
- **Every endpoint requires the header `X-ZoteroJS-Token` except `ping`.** The token lives in the Zotero pref `extensions.zotero.jsbridge.token` and is mirrored to `<data-dir>/zoterojs-token.txt`.
- **The write endpoints do not share a dry-run default.** `apply` and `enrich` write-back are rehearsals unless `yes` is passed; **`merge` merges for real unless `dryRun` is passed.** An agent that assumes one uniform default will merge on its first call. Pass `dryRun` explicitly on `merge`; `apply` and `enrich` default to a rehearsal, so pass `yes` deliberately when a write is intended.
- **It executes arbitrary JavaScript with full library access.** This is a personal automation tool for a single-user desktop machine, not a hardened service. See the security model before recommending installation.
- **`exec` receives Zotero's live global object, not a copy**, so it also reaches whatever other installed plugins have mounted on it. Not every plugin mounts anything, and an `api` object can exist while being empty. See [plugin-interop.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/docs/plugin-interop.md) before relying on a neighbour's surface — and call its capability rather than re-implementing it.
- Runs on **Zotero 7 through 10** — the manifest declares `strict_min_version` `6.999` and `strict_max_version` `10.99.99`. Developed and verified on Zotero 10.0.2. The bundled Python client needs 3.8+.
- The current version is whatever [`addon/manifest.json`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/addon/manifest.json) declares; the latest build is at [releases/latest](https://github.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/releases/latest).
- The repository is [github.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge](https://github.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge), MIT licensed.

## Start here

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/README.md): what the plugin is, requirements, install, quick start, endpoint summary, settings, security model, limitations.
- [README (中文)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/README.zh-CN.md): the same landing page in Chinese.
- [Full corpus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/llms-full.txt): every document below in one file, for ingestion in a single fetch.

## Documentation

- [endpoints.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/docs/endpoints.md): complete reference for all eight endpoints — HTTP methods, parameters, defaults, response shapes, error codes (503 master switch off, 404 endpoint pref off, 403 read-only or bad token, 400 bad parameters, 500 internal). Read this to call the API correctly.
- [merge.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/docs/merge.md): the eight self-checks that must pass before two items are merged, the rule that a missing value is not a conflict, value normalization including every dash variant, and the ISBN check that prevents merging two volumes of the same textbook.
- [enrich.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/docs/enrich.md): metadata enrichment for scanned PDFs with no text layer. Two modes (discovery, write-back), the fill-empty-fields-never-overwrite rule, the three gates, and why the judge is the extracted character count rather than the index state. Also states what the endpoint deliberately does not do: render PDFs or call a vision model.
- [zotero-internals.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/docs/zotero-internals.md): Zotero and Firefox platform traps, each measured rather than inferred. Includes that Zotero 10's `Items.getAll` / `getDeleted` / `getAsync` / `Plugins.getRootURI` are async, that `onlyTopLevel: true` counts annotations as top-level items, the `LIKE` guard that lives in Firefox's `Sqlite.sys.mjs`, and preference-pane registration behaviour.
- [plugin-interop.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/docs/plugin-interop.md): reaching other installed plugins from `exec`, which receives Zotero's live global object rather than a copy. The survey snippet for enumerating what is mounted, the three shapes a plugin takes, and three traps: an `api` object that exists but is empty, `hooks` that are menu actions with side effects, and `data` that is lazily populated so it reads as a confident zero. Also the rule that you should call a neighbouring plugin's capability rather than re-implement it, worked through on Linter's `language` handling.
- [development.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/docs/development.md): contributor documentation — how the test harness stubs Zotero, what mutation testing proves, stub fidelity requirements, versioning, and the rule that a version bump and its GitHub Release must ship together.

## Source

- [addon/bootstrap.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/addon/bootstrap.js): the plugin. Endpoint constructors, the token gate, the `safe()` serializer, and all write paths. This is the authoritative source when documentation and behaviour disagree.
- [zoterojs.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/zoterojs.py): the Python client and CLI. Its module docstring is the canonical list of CLI flags and Python signatures.
- [addon/manifest.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/addon/manifest.json): version, plugin id (`zoterojs-bridge@local`), and compatibility range.
- [addon/prefs.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/addon/prefs.js): every preference and its default value.
- [test_bridge.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/test_bridge.js): the test suite; runs without a Zotero install.
- [mutate.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/mutate.py): mutation testing — reverts each fix individually and requires the suite to go red.
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/AGENTS.md): invariants for anyone editing this repository — never change the plugin id or the pref names, the endpoint constructor and one-parameter `init` shape, auth before the endpoint switches, every write through `doApply`, the five places a new endpoint must be registered, and the rules around stubs and mutants.

## Optional

- [Releases](https://github.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/releases): the `.xpi` builds. Installation is by file, from Zotero's **Tools → Add-ons → Install Add-on From File…**.
- [updates.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/updates.json): the update manifest that installed plugins read; its `update_link` must resolve to a published Release.
- [LICENSE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sum-su/zotero-js-bridge/main/LICENSE): MIT.
